Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 12, 2026. I have worked in Lower Mainland real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Delta.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Before you buy or sell, check the zoning, what the community plan says, and which schools serve the address.

parts.t: These are the questions I go through with buyers.
Lot size, the age of the roof, furnace, plumbing and wiring, and the street

items.t: What the zone allows, and whether any suite was permitted

parts.t: Assuming you can rebuild or add a suite just because a neighbour did
Strata fees, the depreciation report (the plan for future repairs), meeting minutes and bylaws
About upcoming special levies (extra one-time charges) and what the fees include

items.t: Pet or age rules that don’t fit your plans

parts.t: How high the lot sits, drainage, and any rules on the title (covenants)
How high the living space must be built, and whether work on the shore needs a seawall designed by an engineer
Insurance costs or limits. Get a quote before you remove subjects (the conditions in your offer).
Delta adopted a new Official Community Plan in 2024. Zoning and what the plan says can be different for each lot.
Delta’s Official Community Plan is Bylaw No. 8400, adopted by Council on July 8, 2024.

Lots zoned for single detached or duplex homes can have up to 3 units (lots up to 280 square metres) or 4 units (larger lots), plus a secondary suite and coach or garden suites within the unit limits.
Low and waterfront lots may have a rule on the title (a covenant) that sets how high the living space must be built. DeltaMap shows how high homes must be built for flooding.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Tsawwassen East

parts.t: Ask the City of Delta how the property is zoned, and what the plan says about it and the lots around it.
Use the Delta School District school locator for the exact address.
For a strata home, read the documents.
The depreciation report (the plan for future repairs), meeting minutes, bylaws and fees, plus any special levies (extra one-time charges).
Ask whether it was built with a permit before you count on it.
Check the roof, drainage, furnace, plumbing and wiring.
Check flood height rules and the title.
Ask Delta how high a home must be built for flooding, and read the title for any rules (covenants). Also check that the address is on City of Delta land and not Tsawwassen First Nation land.
